text: Dear boys and girls, welcome to my class.Today we are to learn unit 2, animals.First, figure out the organization as well as the general features of an argumentative text.Second, list out the opposing views as well as their corresponding arguments and understand the right stand and the purpose of the text.Third, reflect upon the relationship between humans and animals and raise awareness of animal welfare.First, make sure you've got your textbook and worksheet ready.We will start our lesson very soon.Now please look at the following pictures and think about the two questions here.One, where do these animals live?Are they living in zoos, animal protection bases where animals are protected?Nature reserves where a piece of land is protected for a particular animal, in Chinese, 自然保护区, or breeding bases of animals where animals are born and brought up.Two, how do the animals living in different places probably feel?You can have a discussion with your desk mates.Time is up.As we can see in the picture, the monkey is kept in a cage, in a zoo.How does it look?It looks upset, unhappy, and even angry.What might it be thinking about?It might be thinking, why keep me in the cage?From the outside of the cage, we can hear its inner cry.Let me out, out, out.Now let's look at picture two.The little pandas are living in a breeding base.How are they treated?It seems that they are treated with love and care.So, the baby pandas probably feel happy, safe, and peaceful.Now please look at the last picture.The elephants are not living in a zoo or in a breeding base, but living in the wild, in the open, in its natural state.How are they feeling?It seems that they feel happy, free, and relaxed.Probably because they are in the wild, in the open, and they are able to live in their natural state.They enjoy living in the wild.Well, boys and girls, have you ever visited a zoo?Do you like or dislike visiting a zoo?Do you think we humans have the right to keep the animals in the zoo?Are we doing it for our own sake or for the well-being of animals?The text we are to learn today will tell us people's different opinions on that.Please look at the title of the text.As you can see, the title is in the form of an alternative question.On the one hand, it shows the readers two opposite opinions concerning the very existence of zoos.So what are the two opposite viewpoints?One view is that zoos are cruel.What does cruel mean here?Yes, it means causing pain or suffering.The contrasting view is zoos are caring.Here caring means it means kind, helpful, and considerate.Then on the other hand, the title invites the readers to read the text so as to make a choice concerning this alternative question.Based on the title, can you guess what type of writing is the text?Please read through the text and first judge what type of writing it is.Second, tell what each paragraph is about.You have two minutes for the task.It seems obvious that the text is an argumentative writing.Because an argumentative writing is to convince the readers of the writer's opinion.And in the text, the writer is trying hard to prove to the readers that zoos are a good thing.Now let's analyze the overall organization of the writing by focusing on each paragraph.Paragraph 1 introduces the topic.Are zoos a good thing or not?Paragraph 2 presents the viewpoint against zoos and the reasons.Paragraph 3 presents the viewpoint in favor of zoos and the reasons.Paragraph 4 highlights the writer's favorable opinion on zoos.Here some students may wonder, if the writer wants to persuade the readers that zoos are good, why bother to write about the opposite viewpoint?Actually, it is another feature of argumentative writing.Very often, the writers deliberately touch upon different opinions to show that arguments are sound, logical, and impartial.Now that you have got a general idea of the text, let's dig in and find more details.Please scan the text quickly and answer the following three questions on page 22 in your textbook.If you come across some new words and expressions in the process, don't be frustrated.Try to guess their meanings based on the context.Here is question 1.Why do many people think that zoos are cruel?Why can a trip to the zoo be an educational experience?What is the author's attitude towards zoos?What reasons does the author state?Two minutes for you.One minute for you.Three minutes for you.Four minutes for you.Five minutes for you.Six minutes for you.Seven minutes for you.Eight minutes for you.Nine minutes for you.Ten minutes for
